title: Which choice best describes X / what does the text indicate about X
subtitle: Central Ideas and Details · 11 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **11 of the official questions in Central Ideas and Details are this one** — 3 Easy, 4 Medium, 4 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- The stem says 'Based on the text, which choice best describes...' or 'What does the text indicate about...' and names one specific thing: an exception in a group, a discovery, a newly identified species.
- The answer has to combine two facts or restate a fact in different words.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Collect every sentence that mentions the named item, including sentences that describe it through contrast with the rest of its group.
- The right answer is often a small logical consequence, such as extinct because it is known only from fossils, or the same factor both protected and exposed it.
- 3) Reject any choice that says more than those sentences support.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You describe the group instead of the exception.
You confuse which category the exception belongs to, for example direction of orbit versus shape of orbit.
Or you pick a choice that sounds scientific but is never supported, such as 'frequently studied'.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You describe the group instead of the exception.
